title: Troubleshooting Gurgling Drains and Trap Siphonage
description: When a fixture gurgles or smells of sewer gas after discharging water elsewhere, the primary suspect is often a blocked vent or inadequate drain ventilation. Plumbing traps rely on atmospheric pressure to maintain their water seal. Without proper venting, downstream flowing water creates negative pressure, pulling water directly out of adjacent P-traps. To troubleshoot this issue effectively, inspect vent stacks for physical blockages like bird nests, leaves, or ice build-up. Resolving vent restrictions restores neutral atmospheric pressure, prevents trap siphonage, and eliminates foul odors without using harmful chemical drain cleaners.
